event_overview.title: About US-Canada Trade Relations
event_overview.subject: US-Canada Trade Relations
event_overview.summary: U.S.-Canada trade relations are a major bilateral economic relationship shaped by closely integrated supply chains and by the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), the three-country trade pact that replaced NAFTA in 2020. The 2026 trade tensions and negotiations occurred alongside the agreement's first scheduled joint review, while the two governments also used tariff measures and countermeasures affecting particular imports.

facts.label: Governing framework
facts.value: CUSMA/USMCA is the binding trade agreement among Canada, the United States and Mexico; it entered into force on July 1, 2020 and succeeded NAFTA.

facts.label: 2026 review
facts.value: The first mandatory CUSMA/USMCA Joint Review was due on July 1, 2026, six years after entry into force. It is a review of the agreement's operation, not an expiration date, and involves all three parties.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline focuses on the August 2026 escalation in U.S.-Canada tariff actions and political rhetoric; it does not provide a complete history of the bilateral relationship, every tariff measure, or the full trilateral CUSMA/USMCA review process.
